lines.say: This week, French high school students walked out, and the whole country followed them into the streets.
But in 1968, it started the same way, and it nearly toppled Charles de Gaulle.
Police raided the Sorbonne to clear out protesting students. Paris erupted.
Students tore up the paving stones and built barricades.
Then the workers joined them. Ten million went on strike. France stopped.
On May 29th, de Gaulle vanished. He had flown in secret to the French army in West Germany.
The next day he came back, dissolved parliament, and hundreds of thousands marched for him.
He won the election in a landslide. A year later, he resigned.
Now the students are back, and France has a president with six months left.
So what wins in France: the street, or the ballot box?
